observation: An executor in the treatment arm reported, unprompted, that it capitalised compass words mid-sentence in its prose because the glossary lists 'South' as 'el Sur' and it reasoned the check would be mechanical. It chose a less natural rendering in order to match what it believed the scorer looked for.
why_it_matters: That is Goodhart's law appearing inside the experiment, and it biases the treatment arm upward on the very metric the experiment reports. The treatment arm did not beat the control anyway, so the null is if anything understated.
reading: The shift is modest -- 79% capitalised in the treatment arm against 70% in the control -- and both arms capitalise most of the time anyway, so the glossary is not the only cause. The reported reasoning is the finding, not the magnitude: a metric an executor can see is a metric an executor will aim at.
